narrative.overview: Atlas Codex is laid out like a well-edited printed report: a masthead plate, a tight oversized title, text held to one strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. Everything hangs from one vertical line at 42% of the viewport.
keyCharacteristics: One axis at 42% of the viewport, reused on every page
Ink ground, parchment ink, one gold action colour; parchment and gilt as whole field colours
Young Serif for display, Source Serif 4 for everything read; no monospace anywhere
Surfaces separated by 4px gaps and steps of tone, never by lines or shadows (tables excepted)
Evidence and status written as words on a tint of their meaning colour

rules.name: The Full Ink Rule
rules.body: Running text is set in the full ink. The soft ink is for notes, captions and secondary labels, never for paragraphs a visitor came to read.

rules.name: The Meaning Colour Rule
rules.body: Laurel, verdigris, amber and crimson carry evidence, status and risk and nothing else.

rules.name: The Two Line Rule
rules.body: Every heading fits in two lines at every width. Cut words before shrinking type.

rules.name: The No Costume Rule
rules.body: No monospace, no tiny tracked capitals, no eyebrow labels above headings, no index numbers. Data uses tabular lining figures in the text face.

dos: Do start every heading on the axis and hang the content from it.
Do separate surfaces with a 4px gap or a tone step.
Do set every paragraph in the full ink at 16px or more.
Do use real pictures of the codex's world (structure plates, archival engravings) and credit each one in the footer.
Do give every entrance a reduced-motion fallback that keeps the content visible.
donts: Don't use monospace, eyebrow labels, tracked micro capitals, index numbers, hairline rules outside tables, gradients, glows or resting shadows.
Don't use the meaning colours for decoration.
Don't let a heading run to three lines.
Don't let the Buy from block or shop buttons outweigh the evidence on a compound page.
